not_a_reading: Re-review of existing cleared images and fixed-camera candidate renders; not new independent evidence.

items.finding: North ridge and west cross-gable/cupola share S14.6; the perpendicular stable ridge remains W141. Directly reviewed unchanged-camera overhead after render.
items.limit: Separate 34.1/38.6 ft heights retain local crest occlusion; approximate modern aerial is not a roof-height survey.

items.finding: Chamfered return replaces north-roof tiles on their existing plane and meets the radial hood. Actual master shows the previously missing strip.
items.limit: Exact footprint, seams and stock are reconstructed; other copper/bow correspondence remains open.

items.finding: Southern upper slit moves S21.8 toS19.8, closer to its ca. 1887 photographic position. Other seven centers remain within approximate 1 ft station uncertainty.
items.limit: Camera rests on reconstructed eave heights; exact aperture dimensions and whole-facade correspondence are not accepted as surveyed.

items.finding: Extruded upper apex replaced by pointed cone and lower pitched connector; directly viewed both current master comparisons. Flat street facade and staggered drum remain.
items.limit: Connector height remains camera-dependent reconstruction; this is not whole-house acceptance.

items.finding: Roof tiles no longer cross the three dormer panes; the actual master render shows open glazing, with closed rear host intersections.
Raised courtyard eave clears the formerly intersected upper wall opening; its head is again attached to masonry.
The former approximately0.25m downward offset is corrected at the unchanged section camera. Crest and edge now follow the drawn section much more closely.
items.limit: Exact stock/gutter projection and small finite-perspective residual remain reconstructed.

items.finding: Side overhang reduced from0.26m to0.144m, bounded by native body about445px and roof540px at100.6px/ft. The85mm inset retains the outward lower flare. The revised actual section render is closer in width.
items.limit: Front/back depth and exact stock remain reconstructed. Remaining apron/finial silhouette differences are not final photographic acceptance.

items.finding: The flat shelf is gone, but the coping still continues across the rounded post in projection. The measured section ends nearS45.35 while the circular model path reaches the plan-centred post nearS46.78. T-2759: the plan's wall stays on its circle into the post (inner 17.6, outer 18.7 ft), and the plan's post is larger and sits outward of the band (circle fit W33.81/S46.20, r0.93 ft), standing about 0.6 ft proud of the wall. Built that way, the post's shaft shows whole in the west view and the coping dies into its north side. What remains is a cross-sheet S offset: the section draws the junction at S45.35 with 1.22 ft of clear shaft, while the plan puts it near S46.5 with about 0.5 ft of clear shaft.
items.ruling: T-2879 ruled the plan against the section: sheet 2's printed court chain governs, sheet 4's court is shifted north, not rescaled, and re-zeroed (+0.65 ft) its post reads S46.0-47.3 against the plan-built S46.2-47.1. The post stays on the plan; habs04-terrace-section reads matches since T-2906.

items.finding: Broad barred light replaces the overly low, narrow opening. Source bounds are46.48..50.98S and2.60..4.95ft over grade.
items.limit: Reveal/frame/iron stock is reconstructed; precise local stone surround and tower overlap remain for review.

items.finding: Plan-centred stair tower remains offset from the section projection by about0.63ft; section radius also exceeds the retained plan radius.
items.ruling: T-2879 and T-2925: the stair tower stays on the plan's drum (sheet 2's printed 10'-0" mass), sheet 4 drawing it 11.09 ft across; its lights are placed by angle on the drum. habs04-court-exterior reads matches.

items.finding: Directly reviewed current HABS13 comparison exposes substantial frozen-pose/opening correspondence residuals. HABS14 retains finial/stack and material/lighting differences.
Street openings, entry, silhouette and stone course/lighting differences remain in the early photograph; this roof pass does not resolve them.

T-2760: the west courtyard door is a grade door, 0.35-7.85 ft, its head coursed with the first-floor sills and about 34 brick courses tall in modern058; HABS2's flight descends toward it. No high door, no raised flight.
items.limit: Head read against the record's 7.5 ft sills; the 1904 threshold may sit a step lower in the 1963 plan's areaway, which is undated and not built. See docs/RESEARCH/glessner-west-court-door-T-2760/.

items.finding: Both east-court leaders occupy clear masonry strips beside the revised tower and broad basement light. Full/Light spatial checks pass with no opening crossings.
items.limit: Exact S61.61/42.4ft leader anchors are reconstructed clearances, not independent historic measurements.

items.finding: T-2848: each photographic camera now carries the light read off its own print instead of the review default: HABS 01 a low east-north-east sun (the 18th Street wall raked, the stable's west end in shade); HABS 14 and 15 a hazy sun behind the house to the south-south-west (north faces lit by the sky alone); HABS 13, 16, 17, the Cornell view and Taylor 2135 overcast (nothing in them casts a shadow), rendered with photo_match's new overcast sky. Each camera's solve.light says what it was read from.
items.limit: Sun azimuths are read from lit faces, shadows and flare, not solved from a dated exposure; elevations are not measured. The 1960s HABS prints show soot-darkened stone, which cannot stand for its 1887 tone (recorded as not shown).

items.finding: HABS 13 reads each 18th Street gable pair's lights about equal (east wing about 3.1 ft each against the built 3.35/2.85; tower shoulder about 2.9-3.0 each against 2.65/3.1), the shoulder pair's jambs 15-27 px east of the render's. One print; HABS 14 is the second reading.
The 18th Street gable light's transom stands about 0.3-0.5 ft under the build's in HABS 14, and its fan shows fewer, broader stones than the 11 built (T-3127's handover). HABS 01 resolves neither.

HABS 17 reads the 18th Street stack above the coping's junction at 1.15 of its seen width against the render's 0.95, through a camera about 8 px off the stack; HABS 14 and 01 put the junction at 42.5-43.0 ft ng against the built 43.3, inside T-3024's ruled spread.

Both prints read the Prairie front's first-floor pair over the porte-cochere with its north light about 2.2-2.4 ft and its pier 1.1-1.25 ft, where the build has 2.7 and 0.8; the south light (2.3) agrees. Sheet 6 is the measured drawing to rule it on.
Through HABS 16's camera the render's openings stand 7-20 px north of the print's, growing away from the south corner, while their spacing fits camera-free to 3.3 px (T-2857).

HABS 01's camera is fitted at the Prairie corner and stands 17-35 px right and 30-40 px high at the stable's gable and cupola; HABS 15's roll and loft offset put the hoist about 15 px west. The Cornell camera is fitted at the stable and does not reach the range east of it (great arch about 40 px, stacks 40-60 px off), so the range is judged from the other views.

Both northwest prints show the stable's north-gable pigeon holes round-headed and about a course tall, where the build has 0.45-0.65 ft slits; HABS 01 sets the ledge higher under the apex. The form is attested by two prints; the sizes are readings through hand-solved cameras.

basis_legend.attested: two independent pictures (or a measured drawing) show it
basis_legend.inferred: one picture shows it, or the reading rests on a hand-solved camera
basis_legend.camera: a camera's fit, not the building
basis_legend.scope: carried by the rows T-3136 read (ruled, open); the fixed rows' basis is written with the final acceptance (T-3140)
